s1.syndrome_frame: short stature with skeletal abnormalities and distinctive facial features
salient_findings: distinctive facial features including frontal bossing and micrognathia
skeletal abnormalities including diffuse osteosclerosis and acro-osteolysis
key_facts: short terminal phalanges with bulbous fingertips present
normal cardiovascular, respiratory, abdominal, and neurologic examinations
normal serum calcium, phosphate, alkaline phosphatase, vitamin D level, thyroid function, and insulin-like growth factor 1
skeletal survey showed diffuse osteosclerosis, biconvex vertebrae, a wide open anterior fontanel with Wormian bones, and acro-osteolysis of the distal phalanges

shortlist.label: Pycnodysostosis
shortlist.why_kept: diffuse osteosclerosis, acro-osteolysis, and distinctive facial features match this condition

shortlist.label: Osteopetrosis
shortlist.why_kept: diffuse osteosclerosis is a key feature of this disease

shortlist.label: Sclerosteosis
shortlist.why_kept: skeletal survey findings and short stature are consistent with this rare bone disorder

shortlist.label: Dysosteosclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: combination of osteosclerosis, short stature, and distinctive facial features are plausible for this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Craniodiaphyseal dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: skeletal abnormalities, including osteosclerosis and Wormian bones, align with this condition

raw.rationale: The combination of short stature, diffuse osteosclerosis, large open anterior fontanel, Wormian bones, acro-osteolysis of the distal phalanges, and characteristic facial features such as frontal bossing and micrognathia are consistent with Pycnodysostosis.

rejected.label: Osteopetrosis
rejected.why: While osteopetrosis also presents with osteosclerosis, it typically has a more severe clinical course and often includes hematologic abnormalities, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Sclerosteosis
rejected.why: Sclerosteosis is characterized by syndactyly and a tall stature, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Dysosteosclerosis
rejected.why: Dysosteosclerosis typically presents with more severe skeletal abnormalities and often includes neurological symptoms, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Craniodiaphyseal dysplasia
rejected.why: Craniodiaphyseal dysplasia is characterized by a more severe cranial and facial involvement, often with significant facial disfigurement and neurological symptoms, which are not present in this case.
